messages:
sasha: Pushed a small offline replay run (traceforge) with a new batch-shaper heuristic. TL;DR: token-budget routing + opportunistic coalescing reduced tokens/sec by ~6% but p95 latency regressed ~8ms in a narrow kernel path. Thoughts?
ben: Nice. Can you paste the config you used?
liam: Curious which kernel variant got chosen for the long tails. Could be kernel-selection causing the p95 bump.
sasha: Config below — batch_target_tokens is 256 -> 192 for stage A, queue_policy = 'tokenflow', kv_prefetch = true
```
batch_shaper:
  batch_target_tokens: 192
  token_budget_target: 0.86
  max_wait_ms: 8
queue_policy: tokenflow
kernel_hint: dynamic_v2
kv_prefetch: true
```
remy: Thanks. Which trace did you replay? user-facing chat workload or internal eval harness?
sasha: 2h production trace (anonymous) + the AB harness (50k sessions). The AB harness shows small quality/noise differences but the production trace is where latency shows up.
perf-bot: regression-alert: p95 latency +8.2ms vs baseline on kernel dynamic_v2 when seq>512 (CI job #4821).
ben: Do we have profiler flame for those requests? need to see whether it's kernel DRM or extra memcpy from kv-prefetch.
liam: I sampled a few traces: kernel selection flips to dynamic_v2 when estimated batch mem > 11GB. That path appears to rebind to a fallback GEMM which is heavier for small batches.
sasha: Attached minimal flame snippet (copied):
```
memcpy_gpu: 1.8ms
kv_read_shard: 3.2ms
dynamic_v2_dispatch: 12.6ms
decoder_attention_k: 9.1ms
```
remy: Hm. If kv_prefetch true and seq>512, memory pressure + prefetch copies could push the runtime to pick a safer GEMM. Two ideas: lower token_budget_target to 0.75 for long-seq traces, or force kernel_hint: dynamic_v1 for now.
ben: For the offline sim, can we A/B the two fixes across the same trace set? one variant: token_budget=0.75; other: kernel_hint=dynamic_v1. Keep kv_prefetch true for both.
sasha: Running that now. ETA ~40m for full replay. I'll post the AB metrics.
perf-bot: traceforge-run-2265000000: start. jobs spawned=48.
liam: Also add a microprobe that logs kernel_choice per-request so we can correlate chosen kernel with batch size + kv coldness.
remy: Agreed. If the microprobe shows consistent kernel flip at mem threshold, upstream kernel selector needs a bias term for latency-sensitive routes.
sasha: Will add microprobe and run a targeted 10k-session replay to get fast signal. If numbers pan out we'll propose a rollout: stage 1 reduce token_budget on long-seq routes, stage 2 kernel selector bias.
ben: Sounds good. Thanks for owning. :thumbsup:
remy: ping me once the 10k run finishes, I'll take a look at the flame and help draft the rollout plan.
perf-bot: traceforge-run-2265000042: 10k-sample done. p95 deltas: token_budget=0.75 -> -3.5ms, kernel_hint=dynamic_v1 -> -7.9ms.
sasha: Preliminary conclusion: kernel_hint flip wins more but may cost throughput in some workloads. We'll keep token_budget tweak as conservative default, and gate kernel_hint behind canary.
ben: Perfect. Open a short RFC with the results + canary playbook and link the AB histograms.
sasha: On it. Filing RFC and adding visuals to the replay dashboard.
remy: Nice work all.
